input.quote: The Servicer will not be obligated to provide, license or assign its processes, procedures, models, servicing software or other applications to any Successor Servicer or any third party, or provide anything covered by a restriction on transfer or assignment or a confidentiality agreement or otherwise restricted by legal, regulatory, privacy or data protection policies.
input.rationale: Section 7.5(b) is the only provision in the Agreement that addresses licensing of the Servicer's systems, and it lands squarely in walk-away territory: the Servicer is expressly not obligated to provide, license or assign its processes, models or servicing software to any Successor Servicer or third party, so there is no licence at all to the Issuer, its Affiliates or the contractors/Successor Servicer who would need to run the servicing platform, and no path to add them. That fails both the preferred position (licence extending to affiliates and contractors, irrevocable, transferable to successors) and the fallback (affiliates covered on notice, transferable to a successor). The restriction operates against us (Issuer/Depositor) on a servicing transfer, so it is properly flagged. Our redline converts the carve-out into a non-exclusive, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to the Issuer, its Affiliates and its contractors including any Successor Servicer, transferable to successors and limited to what is necessary to service the Receivables, while preserving the Servicer's legitimate carve-outs for genuine third-party transfer/confidentiality restrictions and legal, regulatory, privacy and data protection limits.

proposal.summary: Replace the Servicer's blanket refusal to license servicing systems with an irrevocable, transferable licence to the Issuer, its Affiliates and its contractors (including any Successor Servicer), retaining the legal/regulatory and third-party restriction carve-outs.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We need a licence of the servicing processes, models and software so that a Successor Servicer (or our Affiliates and contractors) can actually service the Receivables on a servicing transfer; as drafted the Servicer may simply refuse, which leaves us with no path to continuity. We have therefore added a non-exclusive, irrevocable, royalty-free licence extending to our Affiliates and contractors and transferable to successors, while preserving the carve-outs for genuine third-party transfer restrictions and legal, regulatory, privacy and data protection limits.

ops.oldText: The Servicer will not be obligated to provide, license or assign its processes, procedures, models, servicing software or other applications to any Successor Servicer or any third party, or provide anything covered by a restriction on transfer or assignment or a confidentiality agreement or otherwise restricted by legal, regulatory, privacy or data protection policies.
ops.newText: The Servicer hereby grants to the Issuer, its Affiliates and its contractors acting on its behalf (including any Successor Servicer) a non-exclusive, irrevocable, royalty-free license, transferable to any successor to the Issuer and to any Successor Servicer, to use the Servicer's processes, procedures, models, servicing software and other applications solely to the extent necessary to service the Receivables, and the Servicer will provide, license or assign the same to any Successor Servicer on request; provided, that the Servicer will not be obligated to provide anything covered by a restriction on transfer or assignment in favor of an unaffiliated third party or a confidentiality agreement with an unaffiliated third party, or otherwise restricted by legal, regulatory, privacy or data protection policies.
